lines: Plunging your foot into a puddle,
You let out a great big yawn.
I want you to call down a terrible storm,
One strong enough to blow even this sky away.
I was waiting for the wind.
Because a life with nothing in it is surely far too boring.
I was waiting for the wind.
I was waiting for the wind.
Blow, green storm,
And blow even our words away.
So completely that no one can say a word,
Swallow us right up.
Doddo do dodou do,
Doddo do dodou do,
Doddo do dodou do.
“So it is true that you call the wind,”
I said, my eyes wide with wonder.
And you answered me bluntly,
“Everything remains just as I wish.”
I was waiting for the wind.
Because a society fit into a mold is far too suffocating.
“Then bring an even worse rain!
And a wind to blow this mood away!”
Blow, green storm,
Throw everything away.
If we remain just as we are now,
We will end up forgetting even who we are.
Blow away the green walnuts too,
Blow away the sour quinces too.
Grow bigger, terribly bigger,
A wind to destroy this town.
Blow, green storm,
Throw everything away.
All the sadness and dreams,
Blow them all away, Matasaburo.
It is a long road ahead,
And words are your wind.
So completely that no one can say a word,
Swallow us right up.
Doddo do dodou do,
Doddo do dodou do,
Doddo do dodou do.
